title: MafiaScope: Inspecting Multi-Agent Reasoning in Social Deduction Games
abstract: arXiv:2607.10645v3 Announce Type: replace  Abstract: An LLM agent's public behaviour reveals little about its social reasoning: an agent that votes correctly may be guessing, and its public claims may differ from privately elicited assessments. We present MafiaScope, an open testbed that turns the social deduction game Mafia into a measurement instrument for multi-agent reasoning. After each public utterance, living agents privately answer configurable structured questions on copies of their available conversations. Probing is non-invasive with respect to the acting context: neither the questions nor the answers enter the histories used to continue the game. Role assessments are scored against roles known to the engine; second-order predictions are compared with other agents' reports. translated_title: MafiaScope：检视社交推理游戏中的多智能体推理
translated_abstract: LLM智能体的公开行为很少能揭示其社会推理能力：一个投票正确的智能体可能只是在猜测，而且其公开声明可能与私下引出的评估不一致。我们提出了MafiaScope，一个开放测试平台，它将社交推理游戏“狼人杀”转变为测量多智能体推理的工具。在每次公开发言后，存活的智能体会在其可用对话的副本上私下回答可配置的结构化问题。这种探测对于行动上下文是非侵入式的：问题和答案都不会进入用于继续游戏的历史记录。角色评估根据引擎已知的真实角色进行评分；二阶预测则与其他智能体的报告进行比较。交互式可视化器呈现评估轨迹：扮演模式聚焦于单个智能体的信息和报告，面板图表展示时间线对齐的准确率和校准度，反事实……（摘要在此处被截断）
tldr: MafiaScope将社交推理游戏“狼人杀”转变为测量LLM多智能体社会推理的开放测试平台，通过非侵入式的私下结构化提问来揭示智能体公开行为与私下真实评估之间的差异，并提供交互式可视化器分析角色评估轨迹。
en_tdlr: MafiaScope turns the social deduction game Mafia into an open testbed for measuring multi-agent reasoning in LLMs, using non-invasive private structured probing to reveal the gap between agents' public behavior and privately elicited assessments, with an interactive visualizer for analyzing assessment trajectories.
